caption: The drawing is a rectangular, embroidered sampler bordered with pink and red roses and green leaves on all four sides. Inside the border, at the top, there is a line of small red flowers with green leaves, followed by blue embroidered text in the center, which reads: "I do not ask that city spires / May round my mansion rise / But that my home may be where trees / Are pointing to the skies." Below the text, occupying most of the center, is a landscape scene depicting a classical-style building with columns and a triangular pediment colored in shades of tan, beige, and brown, with steps leading up to its entrance. The building is surrounded by green trees and bushes, some light blue-green in color. To the left of the building are two trees, with one being tall and slender. In the left foreground are a grazing white sheep and a brown deer, while to the right of the building is a garden area with smaller plants. Several red birds are perched or flying around the floral border and near the trees. At the bottom, in red embroidery, is the text: "Isabella. P. Burchfield. East. Liberty. June 23 1851." The background fabric is off-white or cream-colored, and the composition is symmetrical, with the majority of decorative elements forming a balanced frame around the central landscape and text.
title: Sampler
